Playbook (accumulated from past tasks):
## strategies
[ace-0002] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: When implementing a money-returning function, check the module's existing helpers (e.g. to_money, round_money, ZERO) and reuse them rather than raw arithmetic; convert inputs with to_money and round the final result with round_money.
## common_mistakes
[ace-0003] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: Guard division-based averages against zero total quantity (return ZERO for invoices without lines) before dividing, and use sum(..., ZERO) with a Decimal start value to avoid int/Decimal mixing.
## domain_facts
[ace-0001] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: In ledgerly, all monetary results must be rounded via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); Python's round() and bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.

item.content: When validating integer inputs, reject bool explicitly (isinstance(x, bool)) before the int check, since bool is a subclass of int and True/False would otherwise pass as 1/0.

Mirror the error codes and message style of existing sibling functions (e.g. reuse BillingError("invalid_state", f"invoice {invoice.id} is {invoice.status}")) so new validation is consistent with the module's conventions.
Don't forget to enforce state preconditions (e.g. only draft invoices accept mutations) before performing the operation; check invoice.status first and raise the module's error type.
